HOME SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Overview of Home Science? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Overview of Home Science.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Overview of Home Science.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Overview of Home Science.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Overview of Home Science.

2. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Kitchen Layouts and Equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Kitchen Layouts and Equipment.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Kitchen Layouts and Equipment.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Kitchen Layouts and Equipment.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Kitchen Layouts and Equipment.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in the Home 2.3 Housing the Family 2.4 Cleanin? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in the Home 2.3 Housing the Family 2.4 Cleanin.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in the Home 2.3 Housing the Family 2.4 Cleanin.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in the Home 2.3 Housing the Family 2.4 Cleanin.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in the Home 2.3 Housing the Family 2.4 Cleanin.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Safety in the Home? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Safety in the Home.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Safety in the Home.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Safety in the Home.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Safety in the Home.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Housing the Family? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Housing the Family.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Housing the Family.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Housing the Family.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Housing the Family.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene During Puberty 2.2 Safety in .

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutritive Value of Foods 1.5 Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutritive Value of Foods 1.5 Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutritive Value of Foods 1.5 Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene .

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutritive Value of Foods 1.5 Methods of Cooking 2.0 Home Management 2.1 Hygiene .

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.

   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutritive Value of Foods.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutritive Value of Foods.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Nutritive Value of Foods.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutritive Value of Foods.
